title: Sortase A-mediated farnesylation of a protein in vitro
author: Sophie Tschirpke

Pipette tips

Tris-HCl

Western blotting equipment
Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) column
To follow this protocol, ensure to have these materials and components on-hand:

Materials: Low-binding tubes and pipette tips: e.g. Protein LoBind Tubes (Eppendorf), Low Binding TripleA pipette tips (Westburg) The farnesyl group easily sticks to plastic tubes. The use of 'normal' plastic tubes and pipette tips will lead to a loss in yield do to farnesyl educts and farnesylated product sticking to plastic. The use of low-binding tubes and pipette tips reduces this loss, increasing the reaction's yield. For analysis: Materials for SDS-PAGE protein gels and western blot analysis (I. anti-His, II. anti-POI or anti-Flag) For clean-up steps 1 & 2: Chromatography columns and operating equipment for size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) and His-affinity chromatography (His-AC)

Set up the equipment and equilibrate the column in SEC buffer supplemented with 0.1% Brij58 ( go to step #4.3 ). Ideally, have the column already ready when the reaction is finished, so the sample can be directly loaded onto the column.
Set up the equipment and equilibrate the column in SEC buffer ( go to step #4.3 ).
Dialyze the Sample into SEC buffer.

Prepare Buffers: SEC buffer : 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH=7.5), 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl 2 , 1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol. SEC buffer supplemented with 0.1% Brij58 : 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH=7.5), 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl 2 , 1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, 0.1% Brij58. CaCl 2 in SEC buffer : 100 mM CaCl 2, 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH=7.5), 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl 2 , 1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol. His-AC washing buffer : 50mM Tris-HCl (pH=8.0), 1 M NaCl, 5 mM imidazole, 1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol. His-AC elution buffer : 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH=8.0), 100 mM NaCl, 500 mM imidazole, 1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol. For the labeling reaction, 'SEC buffer' and 'CaCl 2 in SEC buffer' are needed. Clean-up step 1 (SEC) uses the same buffers as the labeling reaction and 'SEC buffer supplemented with 0.1% Brij58'. For clean-up step 2 (His-AC), 'His-AC washing buffer' and 'His-AC elution buffer' need to be prepared. These buffers can also be supplemented with 0.1% Brij58 if a lot of farnesylated product is lost during this step.

Samples & chemicals: Sample : POI needs to contain a needs to contain a C-terminal Sortase recognition motif followed by a His-tag, and an N-terminal purification tag (that is not a His-tag). Example protein sequences and their construction are given in [Tschirpke et al. 2023]. The steps in this protocol are shown for a POI with an N-terminal Flag-tag and a C-terminal His-tag. The protocol can also be used for differently tagged POIs. However, the presence/absence of purification tags influences the analysis method (western blotting, go to step #2 ) and clean-up strategy used (see go to step #3 ). This protocol utilized that only the reaction educt (Flag-POI-His) and Sortase enzyme are His-tagged, allowing for their removal through His-AC (optional clean-up step 2). triglycine cysteamine farnesyl (might be commercially available, or can be synthesized [Tschirpke et al., 2026]) Sortase A, His-tagged (e.g. Sortase A Octamutant BPS Bioscience ) DMSO Contributed by users 10% Brij58 (Surfact-Amps 58) Thermo Scientific Dithiothreitol (DTT) Contributed by users

Use the spreadsheet Sortase_reaction_calculator.xlsx to calculate the pipetting scheme for the reaction mixture. Reaction volume: If the reaction mixture should be cleaned by SEC ( go to step #9 ), choose a total reaction volume that is close to the maximum sample volume of the SEC column. Example reaction: Pipetting scheme for an example reaction. Steps: Enter the concentrations of existing stocks and buffers: For the Sortase A stock an exemplary conc. of 320 uM is entered into the table - this conc. is variable and depends on your starting solution (yellow cell). For the POI an exemplary conc. of 94 uM is entered into the table - this conc. is variable and depends on your starting solution (yellow cell). Triglycine cysteamine farnesyl was dissolved in DMSO at a conc. of 20 mM (see go to step #5.1 ). CaCl 2 in SEC buffer has a CaCl 2 conc. of 100 mM (see go to step #4.3 ). DTT was dissolved in ultrapure water at a conc. of 1 M (see go to step #5.2 ). 10% Brij58 (Surfact-Amps 58) Thermo Scientific has a stock-conc. of 10%. Enter the final concentrations of the reaction supplements (dark blue cells): The reaction mixture contains 20mM CaCl2, 2 mM DTT, and 1% Brij58. Enter the final DMSO concentration (light blue cell): 22% Based on these values, the spreadsheet calculates the pipetting scheme: Mix 1.5 uL Sortase A, 250 uL POI, 117.5 uL triglycine cysteamine farnesyl (in DMSO). Add 112.5 uL CaCl 2 in SEC buffer, 1.1 uL 1M DTT, 56.3 uL 10% Brij58, 6.2 uL DMSO, and 17.4 uL SEC buffer.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary stock solutions for the reaction.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a fresh 1 M Dithiothreitol (DTT) solution (e.g., dissolve 7.7 mg DTT in 500 µL ultrapure water).
Dissolve triglycine cysteamine farnesyl in DMSO to a final concentration of 20 mM (e.g., dissolve 5 mg in 500 µL DMSO). Prepare fresh for each reaction; do not store in solution.

steps.title: Assemble Reaction Mixture
steps.instruction: Mix the reaction components using a molar ratio of 2 : 100 : 10,000 for Sortase A Octamutant : POI : triglycine cysteamine farnesyl.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the final DMSO concentration is 22%.
Supplement the mixture with 20 mM CaCl2, 1% Brij58, and 2 mM freshly prepared DTT.
Add components in the recommended order: add triglycine cysteamine farnesyl (in DMSO), DMSO, and Sortase A as the last components to avoid premature termination of the reaction.

steps.title: Initial Sampling and Incubation
steps.instruction: Take a baseline sample and incubate the reaction to allow farnesylation.

substeps.instruction: Immediately after mixing, take a '0h sample' (30 µL reaction sample + 10 µL 4x SDS loading buffer/Laemmli buffer) for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Incubate the reaction mixture for 72 h at 4°C under constant slight agitation.

steps.title: Post-Incubation Sampling
steps.instruction: Collect a sample to monitor reaction progress.

substeps.instruction: Take a '72h sample' (30 µL reaction sample + 10 µL 4x SDS loading buffer/Laemmli buffer) for SDS-PAGE analysis.

steps.title: Clean-up Step 1: Size-Exclusion Chromatography (SEC)
steps.instruction: Separate reaction components using SEC to isolate the farnesylated POI.

substeps.instruction: Load the sample onto the column.
Elute using SEC buffer supplemented with 0.1% Brij58 and collect the elution peaks.

Identify peaks: Peak 1 typically contains only the desired product (Flag-POI-farnesyl); Peak 2 contains all three POI species (Flag-POI-farnesyl, Flag-POI, Flag-POI-His) and Sortase A; Peak 3 contains leftover triglycine cysteamine farnesyl and cleaved His-tags.

steps.title: Clean-up Step 2: His-Affinity Chromatography (His-AC)
steps.instruction: Perform His-AC if further removal of His-tagged proteins (Flag-POI-His and Sortase A) is required, particularly for SEC Peak 2.

substeps.instruction: Load the sample onto a Nickel column.
Collect the flow-through, which contains the cleaned-up sample (Flag-POI-farnesyl and Flag-POI).
Optional: Elute proteins bound to the column using His-AC elution buffer to verify the effectiveness of the clean-up via SDS-PAGE/Western Blot.
If His-tagged components remain in the flow-through, use a larger column, reduce loading speed, or load the sample repeatedly.

steps.title: Sample Storage
steps.instruction: Store the purified samples for later use.

substeps.instruction: Add 10% glycerol to the samples and flash-freeze.

steps.title: Analysis and Verification
steps.instruction: Verify the presence of the farnesylated product using SDS-PAGE, Western Blotting, and Mass Spectrometry.

substeps.instruction: Perform Western Blotting using anti-His and anti-POI (or anti-Flag) antibodies.
Identify the desired product (Flag-POI-farnesyl) by comparing the reaction to a control reaction (without triglycine cysteamine farnesyl), which produces only the undesired side-product (Flag-POI).
Confirm the identity of the farnesylated product using intact protein mass analysis at a facility with expertise in lipidated proteins.
